prose: General Intuition, Medal's sister company training spatial-reasoning agents on gameplay video, has raised another $220 million at a $6.2 billion valuation as it starts offering its models for training AI. CEO Pim de Witte calls them a new class of foundation models trained on billions of action-labeled videos, able to act in real time in never-before-seen environments; he claims leading robotics and world-model labs train on less than 1% of the action data Medal's upload pipeline makes available. Medal is on track for three billion uploaded gameplay videos per year, and de Witte notes the sim sees more accidents in a day than the entire USA - a data-density argument for game video as the substrate for embodied AI.
highlights: General Intuition raised $220M more at a $6.2B valuation
Trains foundation models on billions of action-labeled gameplay videos
Models act in real time in never-before-seen environments
De Witte: robotics and world-model leaders train on <1% of Medal's available action data
Medal is on track for 3B uploaded videos per year
'On any given day, we see more accidents in sim than across the entire USA'
quotes: more accidents in sim than across the entire USA
